selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: According to the passage, what two things must happen for the ruler’s purposes in building the palace to be fulfilled?
questions.answer: There must be a teacher who explains the palace, and the people must accept his message and follow it.

questions.question: Why is the teacher’s presence so important in the passage?
questions.answer: Without him, the palace’s meaning would not be understood, so its purpose would be lost.

questions.question: What comparison is used to show what happens when there is no teacher?
questions.answer: It is compared to a book that no one can understand because it has no instructor.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the teacher to the beginning of the palace?
questions.answer: It says the teacher is the reason the palace was built in the first place.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the people’s response to the ongoing existence of the palace?
questions.answer: Their listening and obedience are presented as the reason the palace continues as it is.

questions.question: What change is expected if people ignore the teacher’s guidance?
questions.answer: The palace will certainly be altered and turned into something else.

questions.question: What is the central claim made about the palace and the ruler’s goals?
questions.answer: The ruler’s goals depend on both a guide who explains them and an audience that listens.

questions.question: In this passage, what role does the master play?
questions.answer: He makes the palace understandable and shows its intended meaning.

questions.question: Why would the ruler’s aims become pointless without the master?
questions.answer: Because no one would know what the palace stands for or how to respond to it.

questions.question: What does the example of an unreadable book teach in this passage?
questions.answer: Something full of meaning can seem empty if no one is there to explain it.

questions.question: What does the passage say causes the palace to remain in its present state?
questions.answer: The people’s acceptance of the master’s words and their acting on them.

questions.question: What can be concluded about the people if they refuse to listen?
questions.answer: They fail the purpose for which they were brought there, and this leads to a major change in the palace.

questions.question: What are the two foundations named for the success of the palace’s purpose?
questions.answer: One is the existence of the instructor, and the other is the people’s acceptance of his teaching.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare the palace to a difficult book?
questions.answer: To show that meaning requires explanation if people are going to benefit from it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the master’s connection to the palace’s existence?
questions.answer: It presents him as the reason the palace was established.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the people listening suggest about their role?
questions.answer: Their role is active; they must respond to guidance for the palace’s purpose to continue.

questions.question: What result follows when the people do not pay attention to the master?
questions.answer: The palace will definitely not remain as it is but will be changed.

questions.question: Which is described as the reason for the palace continuing in its current form?
questions.answer: The people’s acceptance of the master’s guidance.

questions.question: In the passage, what two conditions are said to be necessary for the ruler’s aims to be achieved?
questions.answer: A teaching guide must exist, and the people must listen to and accept him.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the master is not a minor part of the palace?
questions.answer: It says the palace would not even have been built without the master.

questions.question: Why is an unexplained book a useful example in this passage?
questions.answer: It shows that meaning can be present, yet still remain useless to people without proper teaching.

questions.question: If the people reject the master’s words, what future of the palace is described?
questions.answer: Its condition will not stay the same; it will certainly be transformed.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect pattern appears in the passage?
questions.answer: The guide’s presence leads to purpose being fulfilled, and the people’s response determines whether that purpose continues.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the link between the audience and the palace’s future?
questions.answer: Their obedience is the cause of its remaining as it is.

title: Secret of the Parable Presence of the Master and Acceptance of His Word
